ambiguities.text: The specification states merge transition block conditions are deleted but does not explicitly state what happens if a pre-merge block arrives during Capella.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume that pre-merge blocks are inherently invalid during Capella since the merge is complete. Any block without an execution payload would fail validation at an earlier stage.

ambiguities.text: The withdrawals field in PayloadAttributes uses 'Sequence[Withdrawal]' without specifying maximum length or ordering constraints in the fork choice context.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume withdrawals sequence follows the same constraints as defined in the beacon chain Capella spec (max 16 withdrawals per payload, ordered by withdrawal index).

implicit_assumptions.description: The proof-of-stake merge has already completed before the Capella fork activates.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Removing merge transition verification could allow invalid blocks that reference non-existent execution payloads to be accepted into the fork choice.

implicit_assumptions.description: The execution engine correctly processes the withdrawals field in PayloadAttributes and returns valid execution payloads.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If the execution engine ignores or misprocesses withdrawals, validators could miss withdrawal operations, locking user funds indefinitely.
